files.README.md:
# exposed-postgresql-repository-commits

Data access layer generated by [DB2CRUD](https://github.com/RaulEstevezA/DB2CRUD) for a database that already exists: entities and table objects for Exposed 1.6.1, repositories and services, in Kotlin on the JVM. It does not create or migrate the database, and it depends on no web framework.

## Settings

- Database: postgresql.
- Entities: written for the tables the input had no class for.
- Services: take and return the entities; updates take a Patch per field: absent, or a value that may be null.
- Transactions: every repository write is committed at once.
- Lists: lists return pages by offset and limit.

## Layout

```text
src/main/kotlin/app/AppDatabase.kt      the connection of DATABASE_URL
src/main/kotlin/app/UnitOfWork.kt       the repositories of every table, and the transaction of each operation
src/main/kotlin/app/errors/             NotFoundException, ConflictException, ValidationFailedException: no HTTP codes
src/main/kotlin/app/entities/           one entity and one table object per table
src/main/kotlin/app/repositories/       the repositories of each table
src/main/kotlin/app/services/           one service per table
src/test/kotlin/app/                    repositories against a database, services on the in-memory repositories
crud-contract.json                      what was written, for CRUD2Controller
```

## Running the tests

```bash
TEST_DATABASE_URL="jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/app" TEST_DATABASE_USER=app TEST_DATABASE_PASSWORD=app gradle test   # a real, disposable database: it is emptied
```

package app

import app.repositories.SqlAuditLogRepository
import app.repositories.SqlCategoryRepository
import app.repositories.SqlCustomerRepository
import app.repositories.SqlOrderLineRepository
import app.repositories.SqlOrderRepository
import app.repositories.SqlProductRepository
import app.repositories.SqlProductTagRepository
import app.repositories.SqlTagRepository
import org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.jdbc.Database

/** The repositories over one database, and its transaction. */
class SqlUnitOfWork(val db: Database) : UnitOfWork {
    override val customers: SqlCustomerRepository = SqlCustomerRepository(db)
    override val categories: SqlCategoryRepository = SqlCategoryRepository(db)
    override val products: SqlProductRepository = SqlProductRepository(db)
    override val orders: SqlOrderRepository = SqlOrderRepository(db)
    override val orderLines: SqlOrderLineRepository = SqlOrderLineRepository(db)
    override val tags: SqlTagRepository = SqlTagRepository(db)
    override val productTags: SqlProductTagRepository = SqlProductTagRepository(db)
    override val auditLog: SqlAuditLogRepository = SqlAuditLogRepository(db)

    /** Every write is committed at once: this only groups the code. */
    override fun <T> transaction(work: (UnitOfWork) -> T): T = work(this)
}

package app

import app.repositories.SqlAuditLogRepository
import app.repositories.SqlCategoryRepository
import app.repositories.SqlCustomerRepository
import app.repositories.SqlOrderLineRepository
import app.repositories.SqlOrderRepository
import app.repositories.SqlProductRepository
import app.repositories.SqlProductTagRepository
import app.repositories.SqlTagRepository

/** What services depend on: a repository per table and a transaction. Every repository write is committed at once; transaction() only groups the code. */
interface UnitOfWork {
    val customers: SqlCustomerRepository
    val categories: SqlCategoryRepository
    val products: SqlProductRepository
    val orders: SqlOrderRepository
    val orderLines: SqlOrderLineRepository
    val tags: SqlTagRepository
    val productTags: SqlProductTagRepository
    val auditLog: SqlAuditLogRepository

    /** Runs work with the repositories of the transaction; commits when it ends, rolls back when it throws. */
    fun <T> transaction(work: (UnitOfWork) -> T): T
}

package app.entities

import org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.core.Table
import org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.javatime.timestampWithTimeZone

/**
 * The "audit_log" table, as the database has it. Exposed never creates or changes it: the database already exists.
 *
 * It has no primary key: its rows are told apart by all their columns.
 */
object AuditLogTable : Table("audit_log") {
    val at = timestampWithTimeZone("at")
    val message = text("message")
}

package app.entities

import org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.core.Table
import org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.javatime.CurrentTimestampWithTimeZone
import org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.javatime.timestampWithTimeZone

/**
 * The "customers" table, as the database has it. Exposed never creates or changes it: the database already exists.
 */
object CustomerTable : Table("customers") {
    val id = long("id").autoIncrement()
    val email = varchar("email", 120)
    val passwordHash = text("password_hash")
    val createdAt = timestampWithTimeZone("created_at").defaultExpression(CurrentTimestampWithTimeZone)

    override val primaryKey = PrimaryKey(id)

    init {
        uniqueIndex("uq_customers_email", email)
    }
}

package app.entities

import org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.core.ReferenceOption
import org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.core.Table

/**
 * The "order_lines" table, as the database has it. Exposed never creates or changes it: the database already exists.
 */
object OrderLineTable : Table("order_lines") {
    val orderId = long("order_id")
    val line = integer("line")
    val productId = long("product_id")
    val quantity = integer("quantity")

    override val primaryKey = PrimaryKey(orderId, line)

    init {
        foreignKey(orderId to OrderTable.id, onDelete = ReferenceOption.CASCADE)
        foreignKey(productId to ProductTable.id, onDelete = ReferenceOption.RESTRICT)
    }
}

package app.entities

import org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.core.Table
import org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.javatime.timestampWithTimeZone

/**
 * The "products" table, as the database has it. Exposed never creates or changes it: the database already exists.
 *
 * CHECK (price >= 0): the services check what they understand of it.
 */
object ProductTable : Table("products") {
    val id = long("id").autoIncrement()
    val categoryId = long("category_id")
    val name = varchar("name", 100)
    val price = decimal("price", 10, 2)
    val status = varchar("status", 10)
    val version = integer("version").default(1)
    val deletedAt = timestampWithTimeZone("deleted_at").nullable()

    override val primaryKey = PrimaryKey(id)

    init {
        index("ix_products_status", false, status)
        index(null, false, categoryId)
        foreignKey(categoryId to CategoryTable.id, name = "fk_products_category")
    }
}
